(p-422) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Qaf.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an.﴾

The thing sworn to (al-muqsam 'alayhi, the object of the oath) is omitted in the verse, and the apparent view is that it is like the omitted object of the oath in Surah Sad, which we have clarified in our discussion of that surah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 2:

His saying here (exalted is He): ﴿Nay, but they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves, and the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing.|"﴾ ﴿"When we have died and become dust? That is a far-off return."﴾ We have already mentioned in Surah Sad that among what is sworn to is that the Prophet (ﷺ) is truthful and that his message is true, as His saying in Sad indicates: ﴿And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾ [Sad 38:4]. His saying here also indicates this: ﴿Nay, but they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾. We have also mentioned in "Sad" that the denial of the disbelievers in their rejection of resurrection (al-ba'th) is included in what is sworn to, and His saying here indicates it: ﴿And the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing"﴾ ﴿"When we have died and become dust?"﴾. The conclusion is that what is sworn to in Sad, by His saying ﴿By the Qur'an, full of reminder﴾ [Sad 38:1], and in Qaf, by His saying ﴿By the glorious Qur'an﴾, is omitted, and it is the disbelievers' denial of the message of the Prophet (ﷺ), their denial of resurrection, and their denial that the object of worship is One. We have explained the verses indicating this in Surah Sad, and we mentioned there that the omitted sworn-to matter in this Surah Qaf includes their denial of the message of the Prophet (ﷺ), as is shown by His saying: ﴿Nay, but they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾, and their denial regarding resurrection, as is shown by His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers say, "This is a strange thing"﴾. We explained the manner of clarifying that by the verses mentioned there and others, and that suffices so that it need not be repeated here.

(p-424) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the earth — We spread it out, and cast into it firm mountains, and caused to grow therein of every beautiful pair﴾ ﴿as an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾.

He, may He be exalted and glorified, mentions in this noble verse that He spread out the earth, cast into it the firm mountains, and caused to grow in it of every beautiful pair, as an insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back in repentance. What this noble verse includes is clarified in many verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who spread out the earth and placed in it firm mountains and rivers, and of all the fruits He placed therein two mates, two in number﴾, up to His saying: ﴿for a people who give thought﴾; and His saying: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see, and cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you, and dispersed therein every kind of moving creature, and We sent down water from the sky and caused to grow therein of every noble pair﴾ ﴿This is the creation of Allah; so show Me what those other than Him have created﴾ [Luqman: 10-11]. Verses similar to this are many and well known.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿of every beautiful pair﴾ means of every good kind among the kinds of plants. His saying: ﴿as an insight﴾ means: We made the earth, cast into it the firm mountains, and caused to grow in it good kinds of plants, in order that We make Our servants see the perfection of Our power over resurrection, over everything, and over Our being entitled to worship to the exclusion of others.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We revive thereby a dead land. Thus will be the Resurrection.﴾

His saying: ﴿Thus will be the Resurrection﴾ means that Allah, blessed and exalted, makes clear that the reviving of the earth after its death, by causing plants to grow in it after their non-existence and disappearance, is a proof of the raising of people after death, after they have become dust and bones. So His saying ﴿Thus will be the Resurrection﴾ means that the coming forth of people alive from their graves after death is like the emergence of plants from the earth after their non-existence, by virtue of the common feature that all of them come into being after non-existence. This is one of the proofs of resurrection (ba'th) on which the Qur'an frequently relies, and we have already presented the verses clarifying this at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, the beginning of al-Nahl, the beginning of al-Jathiyah, and other places.

(p-425) The noble verse says that whoever denies the Messengers, the punishment becomes due for him, meaning it is decreed and established against him with a firmness that does not admit of its being withheld from him. This is clear evidence against what some of the scholars have said, that God may break His threat (wa'id). They argued that He said He does not break His promise (wa'd) but did not say He does not break His threat, and that breaking a threat is good and not evil, while only breaking a promise is evil. The poet said:

"Even if I threaten him or promise him, I am one who breaks my threat and fulfils my promise."

This cannot hold in any case, because God's threat against the disbelievers is true, and it became binding upon them through their denial of the Messengers, as His words here indicate: ﴿Every one denied the Messengers, so My threat came true.﴾

It is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) that the particle fa' (ف) is one of the particles of causation, as in the saying "he forgot, so he prostrated" (sahā fa-sajada), meaning because of his forgetfulness, and "he stole, so his hand was cut off" (saraqa fa-quti'at yaduhu), meaning because of his theft. From this is God's saying: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38]. Thus their denial of the Messengers is a valid cause for the threat of punishment being true and binding upon them. Therefore the claim that it may be withheld is clearly false. What this noble verse indicates is made clear in other verses, such as His saying in this same noble surah: ﴿As for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38]. The correct view is that the word that "is not changed in His presence" (mā yubaddalu al-qawlu ladayh) refers to the threat He made known to them in advance.

As for His saying in the surah of Sad: ﴿Each one of them only denied the Messengers, so My punishment came true﴾ [Sad: 14], from this you know that the threat which may be broken is the threat of punishing the sinful believers for major sins, because God made this clear in His saying: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but He forgives what is less than that to whom He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]. This is in reality a pardon from God for the sins of His believing servants who disobey Him, and there is no difficulty in this. We have explained this in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), in the surah of al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿He said: The Fire is your abode, wherein you shall abide forever, except as God wills﴾ [al-An'am: 128].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Were We then worn out by the first creation? Nay, but they are in doubt about a new creation.﴾

This noble verse is among the proofs of the Resurrection (ba'th), because whoever is not worn out by creating mankind and is not incapable of bringing them into being at first, there is no doubt of his power to restore them and create them a second time; for restoration cannot be more difficult than the beginning. The verses indicating this are very numerous, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who originates the creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27], His saying: ﴿Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79], (p-426) and His saying: ﴿They will say: "Who will restore us?" Say: "He who created you the first time"﴾ [al-Isra': 51]. Verses of this kind are many and well known. We have already clarified the verses that indicate the proofs of the Resurrection, which are frequently cited as evidence for it in the Qur'an, such as the creation of mankind at first, the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and the reviving of the earth after its death, and other things, in various places of this Blessed Book, in al-Baqarah, an-Nahl, al-Hajj, al-Jathiyah and elsewhere, and we have referred to that many times.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in the beginning of Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to conceal themselves from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [Hud: 5].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 17:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the two receivers receive, one seated on the right and one on the left.﴾ ﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watcher, ready.﴾

His saying "idh" (when): it is in the accusative, governed by his saying "aqrab" (nearer). That is: We are nearer to him than his jugular vein at the time when the two angels receive all that proceeds from him. The meaning is that the One who created man, who knows what his soul whispers to him, is nearer to him than his jugular vein at the time the guardian angels record his deeds. He has no need of the books of deeds, because He knows them and nothing of them is hidden from Him. He ordered the guardian angels to record the deeds for other wisdoms, such as establishing the proof against the servant on the Day of Resurrection, as He made clear in His saying: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find laid open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:13–14]. The object of the verb "yatalaqqa" (receive) is elided, and the descriptive term "al-mutalaqqiyan" (the two receivers) is also elided. Its implied meaning is: "when the two receivers receive all that proceeds from man, and they write it down against him."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "Talaqqi means to take in by memorising and writing down," end of his quotation. The meaning is clear, because the angel receives the human's action at the moment it proceeds from him and writes it against him. "Al-mutalaqqiyan" are the two angels who write down human deeds. The noble verse indicates that the seat of one of them is on his right and the seat of the other on his left.

"Al-qa'id" (the one seated): some have said its meaning is "al-qa'id" (the one sitting). The more apparent view is that its meaning is "al-muqa'id" (the one who sits with another). In Arabic it is common to use the form "fa'il" while meaning "mufa'il," as in "jalis" meaning "mujalis" (companion), "akil" meaning "ma'akil" (fellow diner), and "nadim" meaning "munadim" (boon companion). Others have said: "al-qa'id" here means "al-mulazim" (the constant attendant), and whoever constantly or usually remains with someone is called his "qa'id." From this is the saying of Mutammim ibn Nuwayra al-Tamimi:

*Your companion is that you do not make me hear blame,*
*nor wound the heart's sore, lest it grieve and ache.*

The meaning is: "one on the right is seated and one on the left is seated," so the first is elided because the second indicates it. This is a well-known Arabic style. Sibawayh cited in his book the saying of 'Amr ibn Ahmar al-Bahili:

*He shot me with a matter from which I was clear, and my father was clear of it, and for the sake of the well he shot me.*

And the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim al-Ansari:

*We are with what is with us, and you are with what is with you, content, though our opinions differ.*

And the saying of Dha'ib ibn al-Harith al-Burjumi:

*Whoever has his camp in Medina, then I and Qayyar there are strangers.*

So the saying of Ibn Ahmar, "kuntu minhu wa walidi bari'an," means: "I was clear of it, and my father was clear of it." The saying of Ibn al-Khatim, "nahnu bima 'indana wa anta bima 'indaka radin," means: "We are content, and you are content." The saying of Dha'ib, "fa-inni wa Qayyar biha la-gharib," means: "Indeed I am a stranger, and Qayyar is a stranger." This is a well-known Arabic style. The claim that the word in the verse, "qa'id," is the first and was postponed, and the second was elided because the first indicates it, has no evidence and is not needed, as you see. For when the elided term can be indicated by the later one, there is no need to say that the later one is originally the first, and there is no evidence for it.

His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Not a word does he utter﴾, meaning: he does not speak an utterance nor talk a speech except that "ladayhi" (with him), meaning while there is with him a watcher, that is, an angel observing his deeds, preserving them, and bearing witness to them, nothing of them escaping him. "Ati'd" (ready): meaning present, not absent, writing against him whatever he says of good or evil.

What this noble verse contains, that a human has guardians among the angels (*hafaza*) who write down his deeds, has come explained in many verses of the Book of God, such as:

- His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do.﴾ [al-Infitar 82:10–12],
- His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conferences? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:80],
- His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record: "Today you are being recompensed for what you used to do. This is Our record, which speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We were having copied what you were doing."﴾ [al-Jathiyah 45:28–29].

We have already presented the verses explaining this in Surah Maryam, in discussing His saying, the Exalted: ﴿No! We will record what he says﴾ [Maryam 19:79], and in Surah al-Zukhruf, in discussing His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded and they will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:19]. A group of the people of knowledge have mentioned that the one seated on the right records the good deeds, and the one on the left records the bad deeds, and that the companion of the good deeds is trusted over the companion of the bad deeds. If he does a good deed, the companion of the right records it tenfold; if he does a bad deed, the companion of the right says to the companion of the left: "Hold off from him and do not record it against him, perhaps he will repent or seek forgiveness." Some say he gives him respite for seven hours. And knowledge is with God, the Exalted.

* *

**Note (tanbih):**

Know that the scholars differed concerning the deed of the servant that is permissible (*ja'iz*), with neither reward nor punishment for it: do the guardians record it against him or not? Some said: everything is recorded against him, even the groan during illness. This is the apparent meaning of His saying: ﴿Not a word does he utter but there is with him a watcher, ready﴾ [Qaf 50:18], because His saying "min qawl" (any word) is an indefinite noun in a negative context, with the particle "min" added before it, so it is an explicit text in generality.

Some scholars said: only those deeds that carry reward or punishment are recorded. All of them agree that there is no recompense except for what carries reward or punishment. So those who say "only what carries reward or punishment is recorded" and those who say "everything is recorded" agree on dropping what carries neither reward nor punishment. But some of them say it is not recorded at all, and some say it is recorded first and then erased. Some claimed that erasing that and confirming what carries reward or punishment is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: (p-429) ﴿God erases what He wills and confirms﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:39].

Those who said "what carries no recompense is not recorded" said: In the verse there is an elided qualifier (*na't mahdhuf*), whose elision was permitted by knowledge of it, because all people know that the permissible carries neither reward nor punishment. The elided qualifier is to be understood as: "any word that merits recompense." We have already presented that eliding a qualifier when it is indicated is a well-known Arabic style, and we presented that among it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force﴾ [al-Kahf 18:79], meaning every sound ship that had no defect, as shown by His saying: ﴿So I intended to damage it﴾ [al-Kahf 18:79]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And there is not a city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Isra' 17:58], meaning every wrongdoing city, as shown by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We would never destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers﴾ [al-Qasas 28:59]. And indeed among its evidences is the saying of al-Muraqqish al-Akbar:

*And many a fair-cheeked, virgin, slender-waisted maiden, for whom there is dark hair and a long neck.*

Meaning: for her is dark, abundant hair, and a long neck. And the saying of 'Ubayd ibn al-Abras:

*From his speech is a word, and from his deed a deed, and from his bounty a bounty.*

Meaning: a decisive word, a good deed, and a generous gift.

Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed you were in heedlessness of this, so We removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah an-Naml, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾ [an-Naml: 66].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day We shall say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it will say, "Are there any more?"﴾.

Most of the Seven Readers, except Nafi' and Shu'bah from 'Asim, read this word as ﴿Yawma naqulu﴾ with the nun, which indicates majesty. Nafi' and Shu'bah read it as "Yawma yaqulu" with the ya', and in both readings the subject is a pronoun referring back to Allah. Know that regarding the interrogative in His saying ﴿Are there any more?﴾ there are two well-known opinions among the scholars. The first: the interrogative is a rhetorical denial, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ [al-An'am: 47], meaning: none is destroyed except the wrongdoing people. On this view, the meaning of ﴿Are there any more?﴾ is that there is no room for further addition, because the Fire is so completely filled. Some of them cited for this view verses from the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13], and His saying, exalted is He: (p-430) ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."﴾ [Hud: 119], and ﴿He said, "So the truth is, and the truth I say, that I will surely fill Hell with you and whoever follows you of them all together."﴾ [Sad: 84-85]. We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in Surah Ya-Sin, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them﴾ [Ya-Sin: 7], because His oath, exalted is He, in this verse, indicated by the lam of emphasis in "la-amla'anna" (I will surely fill), that He will fill Hell with jinn and mankind, is evidence that it must be filled. Therefore they said that the meaning of ﴿Are there any more?﴾ is "there is no more," because I am already full, so there is no room in me for more.

As for the other opinion, it is that the intended meaning of the interrogative in the Fire's words "Are there any more?" is its request for an addition, and that it continues to be so until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon parts of it draw together into one another, and it says: "Qatt, qatt," meaning: "Enough, I am full." This latter is the more correct view, and it is supported by what is established in the two Sahihs and others from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Hell will not cease to say, 'Are there any more?' until the Lord of Might places His foot in it, whereupon parts of it draw together into one another, and it says, 'Qatt, qatt.'" For in this agreed-upon hadith there is an explicit statement of its saying "Qatt, qatt," meaning "Enough, I am full," and that its earlier saying "Are there any more?" was a request for addition. This is an authentic hadith from the hadiths on the divine attributes, and we have already discussed it thoroughly in Surah al-A'raf and Surah al-Qital. Know that the Fire's saying in this verse, "Are there any more?", is a literal speech that Allah makes it utter. Some scholars claimed that it is like the saying of the pool in the verse of poetry:

"The pool became full and said, 'Enough, enough, gently, gently, you have filled my belly.'"

And that the intended meaning of its saying is what is understood from its state, contrary to the precise reality; we have explained this with its evidence in Surah al-Furqan in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When it sees them from a far place, they hear its raging and roaring﴾ [al-Furqan: 12]. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing, not far away.﴾

His saying "uzlifat" (was brought near) means "qurribat" (was drawn close). His saying "ghayra ba'id" (not far away) carries the sense of emphasis for his saying "uzlifat", whether you parse "ghayra ba'id" as a circumstantial accusative (hal) or as an adverbial of place (zarf). What this noble verse includes regarding the bringing near of Paradise for the God-fearing has come in other places in the Book of Allah, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Hellfire is set blazing, and when Paradise is brought near﴾ [al-Takwir: 12-13], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing, and Hellfire will be brought out for the deviators﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 90-91].

(p-431) Al-Baghawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir of this verse: ﴿not far away﴾ means they will look at it before they enter it.

The Exalted said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more.﴾

As for His words, ﴿They will have whatever they wish therein﴾, we have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surah An-Nahl, in the discussion of His words, ﴿They will have therein whatever they wish. Thus does Allah reward the righteous.﴾ [An-Nahl: 31].

As for His words in this noble verse, ﴿and with Us is more﴾: some of the scholars said: "The more (al-mazid) is looking at the Noble Face of Allah." Support for this is found in His words, ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more.﴾ [Yunus: 26], because "the best reward" (al-husna) is Paradise, and "more" (az-ziyadah) is looking. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And how many generations did We destroy before them, which were stronger than them in might⁠—﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah az-Zukhruf, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might, and the example of the former peoples has passed.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 8]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us.﴾

We have already presented the discussion of this in Surah al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. There we explained that Allah clarified this in Surah Fussilat, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾ [Fussilat: 9-12]. We have clarified this in the commentary on Surah Fussilat.

And al-Lughub (fatigue) means weariness and exhaustion from labor.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾. What this noble verse contains of His command, exalted is He, to His Prophet (ﷺ) to be patient over what the disbelievers say, and to glorify Him, exalted and high is He, with His praise at the extremes of the day, has been mentioned by Allah in other than this place, such as His saying, exalted is He, at the end of Ta-Ha (p-432): ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify your Lord with His praise before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the extremes of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ [Ta-Ha: 130]. His command to him to glorify Him after His command to him to be patient over the harm of the disbelievers is evidence that glorification is something through which Allah helps him to attain the patience that is commanded. The prayer is included within the glorification mentioned, as we have already explained this clearly. We also mentioned in that context the hadith of Nu'aym ibn Hammar at the end of al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾ ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and be among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 97-98]. And we explained there that Allah commanded seeking help through patience and prayer, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45], and the verse continues.

Allah says: ﴿On the Day they hear the Shout in truth. That is the Day of Coming Forth.﴾

We have already presented, at length, the verses that clarify this in Surah Ya-Sin, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and behold, from the graves they will hasten to their Lord.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 50, verse 44:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day the earth splits open from them, hastening; that is a gathering, easy for Us.﴾

Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read this letter as "tashsha'aqu" (تَشَّقَّقُ) with the shin doubled, by assimilating one of the two taa's into it. The rest read it with the shin lightened, by deleting one of the two taa's. His saying, exalted is He: "sira'an" (سِراعًا) is the plural of "sari'" (سَرِيعٌ, swift), and it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) referring to the pronoun in the genitive in His saying "'anhum" (عَنْهم). The meaning is: the earth splits open from them while they are hastening toward the caller, who is the angel that blows into the Trumpet (al-Sur) and calls people to the reckoning and the recompense. What this noble verse includes, that on the Day of Resurrection people come out of their graves hastening to the place of gathering (al-mahshar), heading toward the caller, has been made clear in other verses of the Book of Allah,

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they come out from the graves hastening, as if they were rushing toward a idol-stone they are racing to reach.﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and behold, they will rise from the graves to their Lord, hastening.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51],

• and His saying: "yansiluna" (يَنْسِلُونَ), meaning they hasten,

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will come out from the graves as if they were scattered locusts, hastening toward the caller﴾ up to the verse [al-Qamar: 7-8]. His saying "muhti'in" (مُهْطِعِينَ) means hastening with their necks outstretched, according to the more correct view. ⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Repelling the Illusion of Contradiction in the Verses of the Book):

(p-٣٩٩)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Qaf

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So remind by means of the Qur'an whoever fears My warning﴾.

This verse indicates that the reminder by means of the Qur'an is specifically for those who fear the warning of Allah.

Other verses have come indicating its generality, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 21], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified in it of warning that they may fear Allah or it may produce for them remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha: 113].

The answer is that the reminder by means of the Qur'an is general. However, since those who benefit from it are those who fear the warning of Allah, it becomes as if it were specific to them, as His saying, may He be exalted, indicates: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [51], as its parallel has been mentioned repeatedly before.
